newsitem.title: USA: Korean nuclear group convenes in New York.
newsitem.headline: Korean nuclear group convenes in New York.

text.p: The international consortium working with North Korea to build two light-water nuclear reactors for the communist state said it would convene its general conference in New York on Tuesday.

The Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organisation (KEDO), run by the United States, South Korea and Japan under a 1994 nuclear agreement between Washington and Pyongyang, said in a statement on Monday that the conference would be followed by meetings of two advisory committees related to the project.

Under the $4.5 billion deal, Washington promised Pyongyang two light-water reactors and interim supplies of 500,000 tonnes of heavy oil a year in return for the North's pledge to freeze its suspected nuclear arms development programme.
Light-water reactors are less suitable for producing weapons-grade plutonium.

"The purpose of the general conference, which will be attended by KEDO's members, contributors and other observers, is to report on matters related to the status of the light-water reactor project ... and to report on other projects handled by KEDO," the statement said.
KEDO's executive director Stephen Bosworth said on a visit to South Korea in July that the nuclear deal was on track and building the reactors could start this year.
